title: Jessica Chastain's 'Other Mommy' Trailer Terrifies Audiences Ahead of 'The Odyssey' Screenings
excerpt: The debut trailer for Blumhouse's supernatural horror film, based on Josh Malerman's bestselling novel, played exclusively before Christopher Nolan's epic — and moviegoers weren't ready for the jump scares.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Jessica Chastain stars in Blumhouse's horror film 'Other Mommy', debuting October 9, 2026.
  • The trailer premiered before 'The Odyssey', shocking audiences with intense jump scares.
  • Directed by Rob Savage, the film adapts Josh Malerman's acclaimed novel 'Incidents Around the House'.
  • Nolan's 'The Odyssey' had a record-breaking $264 million global debut, boosting trailer exposure.
  • Universal Pictures released the first trailer for Other Mommy, starring Jessica Chastain, exclusively in theaters before screenings of Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey.
  • The trailer, which dropped online on July 21, features Chastain in dual roles as a mother named Ursula and a sinister supernatural doppelgänger that haunts her eight-year-old daughter.
  • Directed by Rob Savage and produced by James Wan, the film is based on Josh Malerman's bestselling novel Incidents Around the House and arrives in theaters on October 9, 2026.
  • Social media erupted with reactions from startled moviegoers blindsided by intense jump scares before a mythological epic.

An Unexpected Fright Before the Epic

Millions of moviegoers who packed theaters over the weekend to watch Christopher Nolan's record-breaking The Odyssey got more than they bargained for. Before Matt Damon's Odysseus could begin his journey home, audiences were ambushed by the debut trailer for Other Mommy, a supernatural horror film from Blumhouse and Universal Pictures that left viewers gripping their armrests.

The trailer, released online on Tuesday after playing exclusively in cinemas, introduces Jessica Chastain in a deeply unsettling dual performance. She plays Ursula, a loving mother to eight-year-old Bela (newcomer Arabella Olivia Clark), and also portrays a terrifying entity the child calls "Other Mommy" — a doppelgänger that emerges from her closet each night and asks one chilling question: "Can I go inside your heart?"

"I was waiting for 'The Odyssey' to start and then Jessica Chastain's head and contorted body popped out from under a table and I jumped a foot in the air."

— Moviegoer on X
> **"Nolan's epic opened on July 17 to a $264 million global debut."**

What the Trailer Reveals

The trailer opens with what appears to be a tender domestic scene — Ursula coming home on her lunch break, Bela nervously hiding ice cream behind her back. But the warmth curdles fast. Ursula offers to cook scrambled eggs she had already made that morning, then settles on pasta. As the pot burns, she reminisces about when she and Bela "were one person," tears streaming silently down her face.

When Bela's father Russ (Jay Duplass) rushes in, he discovers the entity crouched under the kitchen table, its body impossibly contorted like a spider. The rest is a barrage of disturbing imagery — the doppelgänger bursting through a ball pit, the lines between mother and monster blurring until no one can tell them apart.

![Other Mommy. Key Takeaways Jessica Chastain stars in Blumhouse's horror film 'Other Mommy', debuting October 9, 2026.](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/d/d2/Other_Mommy_poster.jpg)

A Horror Pedigree Audiences Can Trust

Other Mommy is directed by Rob Savage, who earned acclaim for the lockdown-era hit Host and followed it with The Boogeyman. The screenplay comes from Nathan Elston (Succession), while horror heavyweight James Wan (Saw, The Conjuring) produces alongside Blumhouse's Jason Blum.

The film adapts Josh Malerman's 2024 novel Incidents Around the House, which Esquire called "the most purely effective horror novel I have ever read." The book earned Locus Award and Bram Stoker Award nominations. Malerman is best known as the author of Bird Box, adapted into a massively popular Netflix film in 2018.

Joining Chastain and Duplass are Dichen Lachman (Severance), Arian Moayed, Sean Kaufman, and screen legend Karen Allen as Grandma Ruth.

![The Odyssey. The trailer premiered before 'The Odyssey', shocking audiences with intense jump scares.](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/e/ea/Fragment_Odyssee_2245_2.jpg)

Why Indian Audiences Were in the Blast Radius

Universal's decision to attach the trailer to The Odyssey ensured maximum exposure. Nolan's epic opened on July 17 to a $264 million global debut. In India, it collected approximately ₹73 crore ($7.5 million) in its opening weekend — Nolan's biggest ever in the country and the largest debut for a non-franchise Hollywood film, surpassing Oppenheimer's ₹59 crore record. That massive Indian audience, many watching in packed IMAX halls, was among the millions blindsided by the horror trailer.

"The way people during my two screenings of 'The Odyssey' this weekend were screaming during this trailer for #OtherMommy… @blumhouse gonna have a fun hit on their hands."

— X user

What Lies Ahead

Horror Film Highlights
›Directed by Rob Savage, known for 'Host' and 'The Boogeyman'.
›Produced by horror icon James Wan and Blumhouse.
›Based on Josh Malerman's award-nominated novel.
›Chastain's return to horror after acclaimed dramatic roles.

Other Mommy was originally slated for May 2026 before Universal pushed it to October 9, placing it squarely in the Halloween corridor where horror titles historically dominate. It will compete with the survival thriller Whalefall and DC Studios' Clayface, but early audience reactions suggest Blumhouse may have another breakout hit.

For Chastain, the role marks a return to a genre that has served her well — from Mama (2013) to It: Chapter Two (2019). Since winning the Academy Award for The Eyes of Tammy Faye in 2022, she has largely focused on dramatic work, making this horror comeback all the more striking.
